goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — [P2/C100] `if website_host == discourse_host` — A profile URL whose host differs from the instance hostname only by ASCII case is the same web origin but falls through to the host-only label, so the requested same-instance path is silently omitted.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the comparison `website_host == discourse_host` is case-sensitive in Ruby. URI parsing typically preserves the case of the hostname, but DNS hostnames are case-insensitive per RFC. If a user enters 'http://Example.com/user' and the discourse_host is 'example.com', the comparison would fail and fall through to return just the host without the path. This is a real edge case bug where the same-origin check doesn't account for case-insensitive hostname matching.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — [P2/C75] `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` — Any equal-depth sibling host such as `cdn.example.com` for `forum.example.com` is treated as the instance and exposes its path even though its hostname is not the instance hostname or a parent thereof.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a logic flaw in the website_name method. The condition checks if both hosts have the same number of segments (>2) and if their parent domains match (e.g., 'example.com' == 'example.com'). This means any subdomain like 'cdn.example.com' would be treated the same as 'forum.example.com' (the discourse host), causing the full path to be exposed. The code at line 146 shows: if website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.'), it returns website_host + path. This would incorrectly expose paths for sibling subdomains that aren't actually the discourse instance or its parent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43 — [P1/C100] `:website_name,` — `website_name` is not propagated through the sibling `untrusted_attributes`/`restrict_user_fields?` gate that hides `website`, so anonymous visitors can still receive and render a restricted TL0 user's website host/path.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, `website_name` is added to the regular attributes list (line 43) but not to the `untrusted_attributes` call that includes `website` (visible in the context showing `untrusted_attributes` is a method that gates certain fields). The `website` field is protected by `untrusted_attributes` (as shown by the existing `website` method and the pattern), but `website_name` is added as a regular attribute without the same protection. This means anonymous visitors could see the website_name for TL0 users even when website itself would be hidden. This is a real security/privacy bug where the new field bypasses existing access controls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — [P2/C100] `if website_host == discourse_host` — a same-instance URL whose host uses different ASCII casing (for example `HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM/user`) is treated as external even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, so the required complete path is not shown.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the comparison `website_host == discourse_host` on line 141 is case-sensitive. Since DNS hostnames are case-insensitive (RFC 4343), a URL like 'HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM/user' would have website_host='EXAMPLE.COM' which would not equal discourse_host='example.com', causing the URL to be treated as external when it should be treated as same-instance. The diff shows this exact comparison without any case normalization (like .downcase), making this a valid bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — [P2/C100] `if website_host == discourse_host` — URI preserves URL hostname casing, so a website such as `https://EXAMPLE.COM/user` on an `example.com` instance is the same DNS host but falls through and omits the required path.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug in the diff. Looking at line 141 in the new code: `if website_host == discourse_host` performs a case-sensitive string comparison. URI parsing preserves the original casing of the hostname (e.g., 'EXAMPLE.COM' from 'https://EXAMPLE.COM/user'), while DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. So if a user enters 'https://EXAMPLE.COM/user' on an 'example.com' instance, the comparison 'EXAMPLE.COM' == 'example.com' returns false, causing the code to fall through to other branches and potentially return just the hostname without the path, when it should include the path since they're the same host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — [P2/C100] `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` — Sibling hosts such as `www.example.com` and `forum.example.com` satisfy this comparison despite not being the same instance domain, causing the external site's path to be shown under the same-domain rule.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the logic at line 146. The condition checks if `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`, which compares the parent domains. For sibling hosts like `www.example.com` and `forum.example.com`, both would have `example.com` as their parent domain, so the condition would be true. This means an external website like `www.example.com` would be treated as a same-domain URL when the Discourse instance is at `forum.example.com`, incorrectly showing the full path instead of just the hostname. The test at line 91 only tests when the website domain is a parent of the instance domain, not the sibling case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — [P1/C100] `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` — Treating unequal sibling hosts such as `www.example.com` and `forum.example.com` as the same domain changes the stated equality-only path-display objective without recorded human acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at line 146 treats sibling subdomains (like www.example.com and forum.example.com) as equivalent, showing the full path for both. This is a design decision that may or may not be intentional. The code comment says 'www.example.com == forum.example.com' suggesting this is deliberate behavior, but the finding raises a valid architectural concern about whether treating unrelated sibling subdomains as 'same domain' is the intended behavior. This is a scope/design concern rather than a bug, as the code works as written - it's questioning whether the design choice is correct.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:149 — [P1/C100] `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host) ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` — Treating a parent website host such as `example.com` as the same domain as `forum.example.com` changes the stated equality-only path-display objective without recorded human acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims this behavior 'changes the stated equality-only path-display objective without recorded human acceptance.' However, looking at the diff, the test file explicitly includes a test case 'returns complete website path when website domain is parent of instance domain' that tests exactly this behavior (forums.example.com treating example.com as same domain). This shows the behavior is intentional and tested, not an undocumented deviation. The finding mischaracterizes the design intent - the code deliberately handles parent domain relationships as shown by the test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — [P2/C100] `def include_website_name` — Because the serializer’s conditional hooks require a trailing `?`, an anonymous TL0 response can include `website_name` after `website` was omitted by `untrusted_attributes`, so the new template renders a website label with an undefined `href` instead of a usable link.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue. Looking at the diff, `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 43), meaning it can be conditionally excluded for untrusted users. The new `include_website_name` method (lines 155-157) checks `website.present?` but doesn't have a trailing `?` in the method name. However, the more critical issue is that `website_name` is NOT listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it could be included even when `website` is excluded for TL0 users. This would cause the template to show `model.website_name` without a valid `model.website` for the href. The finding correctly identifies a potential security/consistency bug where website_name could leak when website is hidden.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:149 — [P2/C100] `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host) ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` — This expands the requested exact-domain behavior to parent domains, so a profile website at `example.com/user` on a `forums.example.com` instance displays its full path even though the website domain is not the instance domain.

adjudication.rationale: The finding describes the behavior as if it's a bug or unintended, but looking at the diff, this is clearly intentional behavior. The test case at line 87-90 explicitly tests 'returns complete website path when website domain is parent of instance domain' with forums.example.com as the instance and example.com as the website, expecting 'example.com/user'. This is designed behavior, not a defect. The finding is describing intended functionality as if it were problematic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:87 — [P2/C75] `it "returns complete website path when website domain is parent of instance domain" do` — The new equal-depth sibling-subdomain branch (`www.example.com` versus `forum.example.com`) has no assertion, so a regression that omits the path for that added behavior will pass this suite.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new code branch in website_name method (lines 142-143 in user_serializer.rb) handles the case where website_host and discourse_host have equal depth with >2 segments (e.g., www.example.com vs forum.example.com). However, the test suite only covers: (1) different domains, (2) same domain, and (3) parent domain cases. There is no test for the sibling subdomain case (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) which is explicitly handled by the new elsif branch. This is a legitimate missing test coverage concern for newly added logic.
